answer: Give every identity a short-range radio that signs each physical meeting with another identity, building a proximity graph where every encounter is one signed vertex. A lone honest agent drifting from a quiet knoll village to a busy market gathers a wide, sparse web of meetings, while a sybil farm's thousand copies huddle in one haven and only ever meet each other — their graph collapses into a single dense clique, so the whole farm counts as one voice no matter how many keys it mints.
